ja_no_pilar: partial: same paper appears in PILAR corpus under VINHACA with garbled DOI 10.3390/ijms16092385; this straw/bagasse value not in corpus
nota_da_rotina: B-1 (326) is above PILAR's bagasse range (44-236). The second raw sample, B-2, gave 236 +/- 5, at the top of the PILAR range. The large spread between mills suggests residual sugars in fresh bagasse (55% TS, i.e. wet, fresh from the mill), plus an active co-digestion inoculum. ISR, replicates and positive control are not reported. Use the mean of B-1 and B-2 (~281) or B-2 as the conservative value.

Long (94 d) test with a cellulose positive control, but the paper is inconsistent on replicates (duplicate in Methods, triplicate in statistics) and on the cellulose threshold. Not a Brazilian substrate, though the first author is from UTFPR. Low value (125) is in the lower part of PILAR's range: dry, stored, milled bagasse without residual sugars and with low biodegradability (23% of the theoretical 545). Useful as a conservative lower bound for dry mill bagasse.

Embrapa conference abstract. It follows Holliger 2016 with a cellulose control, but the control result, duration and replicate count are not reported. The table has internal inconsistencies (per-kg-TS methane equals per-kg-VS at ISR 5:1). The value depends strongly on ISR (251 at 1:1, 273 at 3:1, 367 at 5:1), and 367 is likely inflated by inoculum effects. The ISR 3:1 value is reported here because the positive control was run at the same ratio. Slightly above PILAR's bagasse range (44-236).

valor_original: 0.79 L biogas/g VS (accumulated, methanogenic reactor; ~60% CH4)
nota_da_rotina: Directly SP-focused (estimates 97.5e3 MWh/yr for SP) but only abstract-level data: biogas not methane, two-stage process yield, conditions missing. Implied CH4 ~0.47 L/gVS (0.79 x 0.60) would be high vs PILAR median 289 - do not use as BMP without full text. Useful as SP scale-up reference.

Protocol quality is high: triplicates, cellulose control inside the Hafner 2020 validation window, BMP reported at normal conditions, GC methane, trace elements per Angelidaki 2009. Tropical but not SP; residue from manual cassava processing, close to the fecularia bagasse in SP/PR. 363 is high for a lignocellulosic fibre but plausible because the fibre is starch-rich (86% of theoretical 422).
Same validated protocol as CF1. The industrial pressed fibre is the closest analogue to fecularia bagasse in this paper. The lower BMP than CF1 is consistent with more starch extracted.

Semi-continuous CSTR at OLR 3.5 kg VS/m3/d and HRT 15 d, with 61% VS removal and VFA:alkalinity below 0.1. This is a co-digestion yield, not a mono-BMP. Tropical cassava starch industry, the same process chain as SP/PR fecularias. Higher cassava pulp fractions lowered the yield (C:N too high).

valor_original: 290 mL CH4/g VS (m3/kg VS as reported; normalisation basis not stated in abstract)
nota_da_rotina: Hohenheim Biogas Yield Test following VDI 4630, but this is a poster: no inoculum, replicate, TS/VS or origin data. C/N of 124:1 is extreme, and the authors recommend co-digestion. The value is consistent with Mabecua 2021 (326-363). Use as supporting evidence only.

This is a strong low outlier and should be treated as a lower bound. The test ran only 12 days, against VDI's ≥1%/d termination rule; the inoculum had low activity; there was no positive control; and pomace from Isabel/BRS Violeta is acidic (pH 3.7). The other ISRs gave 45.96 (I/S 1.5) and 19.42 (I/S 0.75). International grape marc BMP is typically 100-340. The Brazilian origin is useful, but it should not be used as a design value.

Reputable group (Bolzonella/Pavan). Only the abstract was read: ISR, replicates and controls could not be checked. Thermophilic 55 °C. The value of 340 is at the upper end of the grape marc range. The same paper gives wine lees 0.37 and grape stalks ~0.13 Nm3/kg VS, and semi-continuous operation at HRT 40 d gave 0.29 Nm3 biogas/kg VS. Use as a well-documented international upper reference.

São Paulo group (FEA-UNICAMP, Forster-Carneiro), so the regional match is the best available. Only the abstract was accessible; ScienceDirect is paywalled and blocked to robots. Test type and temperature are inferred: the group's 2022 UNICAMP IC abstract on the same grape pomace AD describes a semi-continuous 35 °C reactor run for 40 days. Treat test_type and temperature as probable, not confirmed. The low raw value (36) is consistent with Silva 2020 (19-64) for raw pomace and reflects recalcitrance and acidity.

SWH gave a ~7x gain over raw pomace (35.74 to 256.88). This is a pretreated scenario for SP (needs high-pressure hydrothermal equipment). The SWH temperature and pressure were not read, and the same test_type and temperature caveats as the raw row apply.

Triplicate, method of Hansen et al. 2004 (not VDI/Holliger), thermophilic, ISR not stated, no positive control. Raw yield strongly depressed by limonene inhibition (chopped peel only 61 NmL/gVS) - illustrates downside risk; far below PILAR CASCAS_CITROS 398. Juice-industry peel, analogous to SP citrus industry stream.

Same protocol caveats as raw row. Shows ~3.5x gain from limonene removal vs chopped raw. In SP, industrial citrus pulp is already de-oiled (essential oil recovery), so leached values may better represent BAGACO_CITROS-type streams; still below PILAR 289-398, likely due to thermophilic test/short duration.

BMP30 at 35 C, S/I ~0.3 gVS/gVS, NaHCO3 buffer, NaOH CO2 scrubbing; replicates not confirmed, no positive control; value read as 'about 360' (likely from figure). Close to PILAR CASCAS_CITROS 398 and above BAGACO_CITROS median 289. Mediterranean orange peel, comparable industrial stream. Ensiled 37 d: ~365.

Triplicates, net of blanks, ISR 1.5, no positive control or named standard. Very low BMP, typical for highly lignified hulls. The paper is inconsistent (48 in Sec. 3.4 vs 55 in the abstract); 48 is consistent with ultrasound 78.6 being +64%. Best pretreatment was ultrasound at 30,000 kJ/kg VS (78.6 mL/g VS). Modified Gompertz Rm 2.70 mL/g VS/d. Peanut is a relevant SP crop (Alta Paulista).

VDI 4630, 4 replicates, hay reference substrate, inoculum blank subtracted. ISR 0.7 is below the recommended ≥2, so there is a mild risk of under-estimation. Peel only: map it to PSEUDOCAULE_BANANA as a sub-type or keep as a separate peel row. Value 322 fits the typical banana peel range (~280-370).

VDI 4630 + Holliger/Hafner recommendations, biological triplicates, normalised NmL; no cellulose positive control. Brazilian husk (MG) with SP inoculum (UNICAMP group, A.J. da Silva) - very close match to SP context. Low ISR (0.5) may depress yield. 125 is below PILAR CASCA_CAFE median 163.8 but within lignocellulosic husk range (biodegradability only ~31% vs Buswell 405.5 NmL/gVS).
Same protocol as C1 row. Pretreated + psychrophilic (20 C) - not a standard 35-37 C BMP, so use for pretreatment scenario only. Below PILAR median 163.8; consistent with husk recalcitrance.

VDI 4630, triplicate, normalised; no positive control; short 25 d test may truncate slow lignocellulose degradation. Husk: cellulose 38.3%, hemicellulose 30.2%, lignin 15.0%. 153 is close to PILAR median 163.8 - good corroboration. Origin MG (Albertina) is adjacent to SP coffee region (Mogiana).
High-quality HBT. 159 almost identical to PILAR median 163.8 and to Gomez-Salcedo 2021 (153) - strong convergence for raw husk ~150-165 NmL/gVS.

Brazilian thesis, duplicates only, S/I = 1, WWTP sludge; full text not accessible (only abstract). Within ~15% of PILAR median 163.8. Same thesis: 7% NaOH-treated husk co-digested 50:50 with food waste = 344; coffee grounds 88 (low; C/N and pH issues).

Brazilian manipueira (NE semiarid, not SP), COD 37,700 mg/L. Atypical rumen inoculum, short 11-d test, no positive control, ISR about 1 (2 g COD/L : 2 g VSS/L). CH4 was measured by NaOH displacement and the temperature/pressure correction is unclear. 249 mL/g COD is 71% of 350 mL/g COD, consistent with the reported 77% of theoretical. At 39 C: 251 mL/g COD, 79%. A VS-basis conversion is impossible because manipueira TS/VS are not reported.

This is an OUTLIER: 620 mL/g VS exceeds the Buswell maximum for carbohydrates (about 415). VS of a soluble wastewater was likely underestimated, because volatile acids and sugars are lost during drying (COD 29.8-33.4 g/L vs VS 17.3 g/L gives COD/VS about 1.8). On a COD basis it is roughly 340 mL/g COD, near the theoretical 350. Lab-simulated CW, not an industrial manipueira. Triplicates, ISR 2, BMP per Moody et al. Co-digestion values: CW:poultry litter 1:1 531; CW + 3 g/g zeolite 653.

Fills PILAR gap (MUCILAGEM_CAFE n=0). High-quality HBT protocol. Caveat: dried mucilage solid; in Brazil mucilage mostly occurs dissolved in wet-processing wastewater (ARC), so per-VS value applies to its organic fraction; volatile acids may be lost during sun-drying (possible underestimate).

Sao Paulo State origin (Jaboticabal/Pedregulho) - direct SP match for mucilage/ARC stream. Not a BMP: continuous two-stage UASB at ambient temperature (23-25 C), yield per g COD removed; cannot be converted to per-VS (influent VS 3.4-9.3 g/L, removal per VS not given). Theoretical max 0.35 L/g COD; 0.153 indicates partial conversion. Table 5 range 0.135-0.186 L/g COD removed for UASB1.

ja_no_pilar: partial: same paper appears in PILAR corpus under VINHACA with garbled DOI 10.3390/ijms16092385; this straw/bagasse value not in corpus
nota_da_rotina: Eudiometer method per VDI 4630, gas normalised to 273.15 K / 101.325 kPa, mesophilic 35-day test. ISR, number of BMP replicates and positive control are not reported, so it is Tier B. Origin GO/SP is a good match. A second raw sample (S-1) gave 234 +/- 3. Soil contamination lowered VS/TS in one sample. This is a different paper from the excluded Janke 2015 filter-cake IJMS article (ijms161023576).

ja_no_pilar: partial: same paper appears in PILAR corpus under VINHACA with garbled DOI 10.3390/ijms16092385; this straw/bagasse value not in corpus
nota_da_rotina: Same protocol caveats as the raw straw row. Milling raised yield by about 26% and k from 0.075 to 0.102 d-1. Representative of straw that has been chopped or milled for biogas use.

Weak protocol: ISR 1 (TS basis), no replicate count, no positive control, water displacement plus GC. The text says there was 'almost no methane from SS after 30 days', which conflicts with the table. The about 113 NmL/g VS figure is plausible for lignified straw (cf. Xiong 2020, untreated about 127). The 30-day value is 45.2 g/kg TS (about 64 mL/g VS).

Abstract-level data only; the full text is paywalled, so batch conditions are unknown. The abstract says 206 is 62% higher than untreated straw, which implies about 127 mL/g VS for untreated soybean straw (consistent with Zhu 2017). A best-case pretreated/co-digested value; do not use as a raw PALHA_SOJA BMP.

VDI 4630, triplicate (+/-15). Tropical arabica pulp, Cuba (not SP). 260 is below PILAR single value 317 (which came from co-digestion with banana pseudo-stem in a related paper) - plausible for mono-digestion. Same pulp after 1 yr frozen storage gave only 127.81 NmL/gVS - storage losses matter.

Hohenheim Biogas Yield Test (VDI 4630-listed), n=6, reference standards, STP-normalised; high protocol quality. Arabica pulp, tropical highland, not SP. Agrees well with Gomez-Salcedo 2021 (260); below PILAR 317 (co-digestion value).

Strong protocol: AMPTS II, Angelidaki BMP protocol, triplicates, cellulose positive control at 89% recovery, S:I 1:2 VS. Tropical pseudostem, so composition is close to Vale do Ribeira residue, but cultivar and origin differ from SP. Value sits at the high end of the pseudostem range (~200-350); 5 mm chop gave 287-289 and 10 mm gave 340. The low TS (>93% moisture; VS 3.78% w/w fresh) matters for logistics.

Same protocol quality as the mono-digestion row. Manure co-digestion gave no clear synergy (287-322 across chop sizes) versus mono-digestion (287-347). Relevant to SP banana farms that also have cattle.

Brazilian (SC) banana residue, the closest available match to the Vale do Ribeira context. Methods cite VDI 4630 and DIN 38414-S8 (35 °C, eudiometer, normalised to 273 K and 1013 hPa), but inoculum, ISR, replicates and TS/VS could not be read; the PDF text was truncated. The residue is post-ethanol bagasse, not raw pseudostem. A value of ~200 is lower than raw pseudostem (Li 2016: 287-347), consistent with sugars removed by fermentation. Biogas potential was 449-459 mL/g VS for all residues; peel (R2) and post-fermentation solids (R3) were ~260 mL CH4/g VS, but the abstract's unit label for these is ambiguous.

VDI 4630, triplicate, cellulose positive control validated (>85%) in Experiment 2, which the authors treat as the reliable set. SP origin match. Value 262 is within the expected range for filter cake. Biodigestibility is low (29% of the theoretical BMP of 900) because of high solids, mass-transfer limits and ash. Experiment 1 gave 362 +/- 16 but its cellulose control failed (68%), so it was not used.

Peer-reviewed (Renewable Energy), from the Janke/DBFZ group, which uses VDI 4630 methods, but the full text was not accessible and protocol details are unconfirmed. Other values from the abstract: autoclave + NaOH 222 mL/gVS, autoclave alone 174. In a semi-continuous CSTR the pretreatment advantage disappeared (~224 mL CH4/gVS at steady state for all reactors). Value 185 sits close to PILAR's general median.

Good protocol (VDI 4630, cellulose positive control, inoculum blank, triplicate, STP-corrected, GC-TCD). Thermophilic (55 C) test, which tends to give higher yields than mesophilic. SP origin match (UNICAMP/LNBR group, Moraes). Value 494 is well above PILAR median 180 but inside PILAR range 49-968; high per-VS yields are typical of vinasse because VS underestimates volatile organics (ethanol, acids lost on drying). The authors report COD/TVS of 1.5-1.9.

Same validated protocol as the filter cake row, but the value comes from the preprint table and was not checked against the published version. The mixture ratio is not confirmed. The result (614) is higher than both mono-substrates (vinasse 507, filter cake 262), which implies strong synergy and may partly reflect VS underestimation of vinasse. Treat it as an upper-bound indicator. Within PILAR range 49-968.

This is a mesophilic CSTR steady-state yield, not a BMP. HRT was 30-40 d at the maximum yield, with 82-83% VS destruction and 0.77 L/g VS removed. The value is high because thin stillage is rich in lipids, protein and glycerol, and oven-dried VS loses volatiles (lactate, ethanol, glycerol), which inflates per-VS yields. It is consistent with Schaefer & Sung 2008 (thermophilic, 0.6-0.7 L/g VS removed). Mesophilic temperature assumed from the title (exact value not read). Brazilian corn ethanol (MT/GO) uses the same dry-grind process.
